name: claude-skills
description: A collection of Claude Code skills and plugins.

plugins.name: data-analysis
plugins.description: Two skills for a data science project's raw data. review re-derives findings from the raw data and code, then checks whether the project's stated conclusions hold up and lists what the data supports that the project never claimed. discover starts from a business decision, its metric and a baseline, and rates the patterns the data supports without claiming causes. All analysis, including code execution, runs on a disposable copy of the project, so the original is never modified.

plugins.name: ciso
plugins.description: Organizes work toward security certifications (HITRUST CSF, SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, CMMC or your own framework) alongside the work that satisfies them: register, import a controls list, interview, review a PR, attach evidence, audit readiness, all tracked in local HTML dashboards. Ships structural control metadata, plus verbatim requirement text only where the publisher's work carries no copyright (CMMC); licensed wording is imported per-org at runtime and never stored in this repo.

plugins.name: docs-warden
plugins.description: Keeps repository documentation consistent and honest. Scaffolds a document set scaled by repo archetype, audits for missing, stale or off-standard docs, and regenerates generated docs so drift from the code is reported, not discovered. Ships a plain-English Vale style, a domain-model skill, and optional compliance overlays (IEC 62304, OSPS Baseline, EU CRA, NIST SSDF) that describe document structure only and never invent regulatory content.

plugins.name: fabflows
plugins.description: Routes work from an expensive lead model to tool-scoped workers on Haiku, Sonnet and Opus, and makes the lead re-verify their reports. Adds a build loop where an Opus builder implements a spec and fresh reviewers return ACCEPT or REWORK, brainstorming to write that spec, tickets in GitHub Issues, Jira or Linear, and audit trace reports. An ACTIVE guard hook asks before package installs and blocks default-branch commits, destructive commands and credential-file access. It fails open.
